theme: “I AM the light of the world”; before Abraham was, I AM
readingInstruction: Read John 8:12-59. Jesus declares himself the light of the world and argues with the leaders about freedom, fatherhood, and Abraham. It ends with the strongest claim to deity in the Gospel. Notice the “I AM” in verse 58.
settingTheScene: The conflict at the Feast of Booths continues. The lamps in the temple courts would have been burning, and Jesus calls himself the light of the world. The discussion that follows grows heated, with the Jews claiming to be Abraham’s children and free, and Jesus pointing out that they are slaves to sin. It ends with Jesus saying the divine name over himself, and the crowd picking up stones.
observation: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life” (8:12).
“And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free” (8:32).
“Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin” (8:34).
“So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed” (8:36).
“You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father’s desires” (8:44).
“Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day. He saw it and was glad” (8:56).
“Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am” (8:58).
“So they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple” (8:59).
interpretation:
“I am the light of the world.” This is the second of John’s seven “I AM” statements (after the bread of life). The Old Testament pictures God as light, and as the one who led Israel with a pillar of fire. Whoever follows Jesus will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life. The Pharisees object that Jesus is bearing witness about himself, and he answers that his Father also bears witness.

Then he says, “You will die in your sins unless you believe that I am he.” This is the first of several uses of “I am” in the chapter. To the believers among them, he says, “If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.” The Jews bristle: we are Abraham’s offspring and have never been enslaved. Jesus replies that everyone who sins is a slave to sin, and that only the Son can set them free. Freedom comes only from him.

The argument escalates. They claim Abraham as their father, and Jesus tells them Abraham would not have acted as they do. They claim God as their father, and Jesus says that if God were their Father, they would love him. Instead they are acting like the devil, who was a murderer from the beginning and a liar. These are harsh words, spoken to those who were trying to kill him.

Finally, they ask, “Are you greater than our father Abraham?” Jesus replies, “Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day.” They are incredulous: “You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?” Then comes the verse: “Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am.” He does not say “I was.” He uses the divine name from Exodus 3:14. The leaders understand exactly what he is claiming, and they pick up stones. It is blasphemy unless it is true.

The chapter shows that the issue is not just Jesus’ teaching but his identity. If he is the eternal I AM, then he is the light, the truth, and the one who can set us free.
connection: Exodus 3:14 is God’s name, I AM. Isaiah 41:4 and 43:10-13 also use “I am he.” Psalm 27:1 says the LORD is my light. Isaiah 9:2 and 60:1-3 promise light to those in darkness. John 1:4-9 says the Word is the light. Romans 6:16-18 explains slavery to sin and freedom in Christ. Galatians 5:1 says for freedom Christ has set us free. Hebrews 11:13 says the patriarchs saw the promises from afar. 1 John 1:5-7 says God is light.
application:
Ask where you still walk in darkness. Bring that area to Jesus, the light.

What are you enslaved to? Bring it to the Son, who makes you free indeed.

Pray, “Jesus, you are the I AM,” and let the weight of that rest on you.
prayerPrompts: Tell Jesus you want to follow the light of the world.
Ask him to set you free from sin by his truth.
Worship him as the great I AM.
